parents.text: # Acme Corporation - Onboarding Guide for New Engineers ## First Week Checklist Welcome to the engineering team at Acme Corporation! During your first week, please complete the following steps: 1. Set up your development environment using the Engineering Setup Guide located on the internal wiki at wiki.acmecorp.com/engineering/setup. 2. Request access to the company GitHub organization by emailing devops@acmecorp.com with your GitHub username. 3. Complete the mandatory Security Awareness Training module in the Learning Management System (LMS). This must be finished within your first 5 business days. 4. Schedule a 1-on-1 with your assigned mentor. Your mentor will be introduced to you by your manager on your first day. 5. Join the following Slack channels: #engineering, #engineering-help, #deploy-notifications, and your team-specific channel. ## Development Standards All code at Acme Corporation must follow these standards: - Code must be reviewed by at least one peer before merging to the main branch. - All pull requests must include unit tests with a minimum of 80% code coverage for new code. - Commit messages must follow the Conventional Commits format (e.g., "feat: add user login endpoint"). - All services must include health check endpoints at /health and /ready. - API documentation must be maintained in OpenAPI 3.0 format. ## Deployment Process Acme uses a continuous delivery pipeline managed through Jenkins. The deployment process works as follows: 1. Developers push code to a feature branch and open a pull request. 2. Automated tests run in the CI pipeline. All tests must pass before merging. 3. After merge to main, the code is automatically deployed to the staging environment. 4. QA engineers perform manual testing on staging for 24 hours. 5. After QA approval, the release manager promotes the build to production using the deployment dashboard at deploy.acmecorp.com. 6. Production deployments are only allowed Monday

3. After merge to main, the code is automatically deployed to the staging environment. 4. QA engineers perform manual testing on staging for 24 hours. 5. After QA approval, the release manager promotes the build to production using the deployment dashboard at deploy.acmecorp.com. 6. Production deployments are only allowed Monday through Thursday, between 10:00 AM and 2:00 PM EST. No deployments are permitted on Fridays or the day before company holidays. ## On-Call Rotation All engineers participate in the on-call rotation. Each rotation lasts one week, from Monday 9:00 AM to the following Monday 9:00 AM. On-call engineers must: - Acknowledge production alerts within 15 minutes - Begin investigation within 30 minutes - Escalate to the team lead if the issue is not resolved within 2 hours - Write a post-mortem document for any incident lasting longer than 1 hour On-call compensation is an additional $500 per week. If called outside business hours, engineers receive an additional $100 per incident responded to.

# Acme Corporation - Employee Handbook ## Remote Work Policy Acme Corporation allows all full-time employees to work remotely up to 3 days per week. Remote work days must be approved by the employee's direct manager at least 48 hours in advance. Employees working remotely are expected to be available on Slack between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM in their local time zone. Employees who wish to work fully remote must submit a formal request to the Human Resources department. Fully remote arrangements are reviewed on a quarterly basis and may be revoked if performance metrics are not met. ## Paid Time Off (PTO) All full-time employees receive 20 days of paid time off per year, accrued at a rate of 1.67 days per month. PTO requests must be submitted through the HR portal at least two weeks before the requested dates. Managers have 3 business days to approve or deny PTO requests. Unused PTO can be carried over to the next calendar year, up to a maximum of 5 days. Any PTO beyond this limit will be forfeited on January 1st. Employees who leave the company will be paid out for any unused, accrued PTO at their current daily rate. ## Parental Leave Acme Corporation provides 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave for all new parents, regardless of gender. This applies to birth, adoption, and foster care placements. Parental leave must begin within 12 months of the qualifying event. Employees may choose to take parental leave in two separate blocks, with manager approval. ## Health Insurance Acme Corporation offers three health insurance plans: Bronze, Silver, and Gold. The company covers 80% of the premium for the Silver plan, which is the default enrollment option. Employees may upgrade to the Gold plan by paying the difference, approximately $150 per

separate blocks, with manager approval. ## Health Insurance Acme Corporation offers three health insurance plans: Bronze, Silver, and Gold. The company covers 80% of the premium for the Silver plan, which is the default enrollment option. Employees may upgrade to the Gold plan by paying the difference, approximately $150 per month. Dental and vision coverage are included at no additional cost in all plans. Open enrollment occurs annually during the month of November. Life changes such as marriage, birth of a child, or relocation allow for mid-year enrollment changes within 30 days of the qualifying event. ## Performance Reviews Performance reviews are conducted semi-annually in June and December. Each review consists of a self-assessment, peer feedback from at least two colleagues, and a manager evaluation. Ratings are on a scale of 1 to 5, where 3 indicates "Meets Expectations" and 5 indicates "Exceptional Performance." Employees who receive a rating of 4 or above are eligible for a merit-based salary increase of 3% to 8%. Employees who receive a rating below 2 for two consecutive review periods will be placed on a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) lasting 90 days. ## Expense Reimbursement Business expenses must be submitted through the expense portal within 30 days of the transaction. Receipts are required for all expenses over $25. The following categories have pre-approved limits: - Meals during business travel: up to $75 per day - Hotel accommodations: up to $200 per night - Ground transportation: up to $50 per day - Conference registration: up to $2,000 per event per year Reimbursements are processed within 10 business days and deposited directly into the employee's paycheck.

# Acme Corporation - IT Security Policy ## Password Requirements All employees must use passwords that are at least 14 characters long and include a mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters. Passwords must be changed every 90 days. The system will not allow reuse of the last 12 passwords. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is mandatory for all company systems, including email, VPN, and cloud applications. ## Data Classification Acme Corporation classifies data into four levels: 1. Public: Information intended for public release, such as marketing materials. 2. Internal: General business information not intended for public disclosure, such as internal memos. 3. Confidential: Sensitive business data including financial reports, strategic plans, and employee records. 4. Restricted: Highly sensitive data such as trade secrets, customer payment information, and access credentials. Confidential and Restricted data must be encrypted at rest and in transit. Sharing of Restricted data outside the organization requires written approval from the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO). ## Acceptable Use Policy Company devices and networks are provided for business purposes. Limited personal use is permitted as long as it does not interfere with work responsibilities or violate any company policies. Employees must never: - Install unauthorized software on company devices - Connect personal USB storage devices to company computers - Access or store inappropriate or illegal content on company systems - Share login credentials with anyone, including IT staff ## Incident Reporting All security incidents must be reported to the IT Security team within 1 hour of discovery by emailing security@acmecorp.com or calling the Security Hotline at extension 4455. Examples of security incidents include suspected phishing emails, unauthorized access attempts, lost or stolen devices, and suspected malware infections. The IT Security team will classify the incident and respond within 4 hours for Critical incidents and 24 hours

Examples of security incidents include suspected phishing emails, unauthorized access attempts, lost or stolen devices, and suspected malware infections. The IT Security team will classify the incident and respond within 4 hours for Critical incidents and 24 hours for Medium severity incidents. Failure to report a known security incident is a violation of company policy and may result in disciplinary action. ## Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) Employees may use personal devices for work purposes only after enrolling them in the Mobile Device Management (MDM) system. Personal devices must have a screen lock enabled, full-disk encryption, and up-to-date operating systems. The company reserves the right to remotely wipe corporate data from personal devices if the device is lost, stolen, or if the employee leaves the company.

The Legend of the Clockwork Fox In the village of Thornhaven, nestled between the Amber Mountains and the Whispering Forest, there lived an old watchmaker named Elara. She was known throughout the region for crafting timepieces so precise that sailors used them to navigate by the stars. But Elara had a secret project hidden beneath her workshop: a mechanical fox made of brass gears, copper springs, and sapphire eyes. Elara had spent seventeen years building the clockwork fox. She called it Fennick. Unlike her clocks, which merely counted time, Fennick could think. He could solve puzzles, remember faces, and even tell jokes, though his humor was rather dry and mechanical. Fennick's brain was a marvel of miniature engineering: three thousand interlocking gears arranged in a pattern Elara had discovered in an ancient manuscript found in the ruins of the Old Library. One autumn evening, a merchant named Valdric arrived in Thornhaven carrying a peculiar gemstone. It was the Heartstone of Meridia, a legendary ruby said to grant its owner the ability to understand any language, human or animal. Valdric offered the stone to whoever could solve an impossible riddle: "What walks without legs, speaks without a mouth, and remembers without a mind?" The villagers puzzled over the riddle for days. The blacksmith guessed "the wind." The baker guessed "a river." The schoolteacher guessed "a shadow." None were correct. On the third night, Fennick emerged from Elara's workshop, his brass paws clicking softly on the cobblestones. He approached Valdric and spoke in his precise, ticking voice: "The answer is a clock. A clock walks through time without legs, speaks the hour without a mouth, and remembers every moment without a mind." Valdric was stunned. He had never seen a mechanical creature that could reason. He handed the Heartstone to Elara, who

in his precise, ticking voice: "The answer is a clock. A clock walks through time without legs, speaks the hour without a mouth, and remembers every moment without a mind." Valdric was stunned. He had never seen a mechanical creature that could reason. He handed the Heartstone to Elara, who placed it carefully into a compartment in Fennick's chest. Something remarkable happened: Fennick's sapphire eyes glowed warmly, and for the first time, he laughed. Not a mechanical clicking sound, but a genuine, warm laugh. From that day forward, Fennick became Thornhaven's most beloved resident. He helped the farmers predict weather patterns by analyzing barometric pressure changes in his internal sensors. He tutored children in mathematics using his gear-based calculation engine. And every evening, he would sit by the village fountain and tell stories, each one woven from the thousands of conversations he had recorded and remembered throughout the day. But Fennick never forgot that he was a machine. When children asked him if he was alive, he would pause his gears thoughtfully and say, "I don't know if I am alive. But I know that I care about you, and perhaps that is close enough." Elara lived to the age of ninety-three. In her final days, she gave Fennick her workshop and all her tools. "You are my greatest invention," she told him. "Not because you can think, but because you choose to be kind." Fennick maintained the workshop for another hundred years, repairing clocks by day and telling stories by night. And somewhere in his chest, the Heartstone continued to glow, a reminder that even things made of metal and gears can carry something very much like a soul.

The Deep Sea Expedition of the Nautilus VII Captain Mireya Solano had always dreamed of reaching the Abyssal Trench, the deepest point in the Southern Ocean at 11,034 meters below sea level. On March 15th, 2024, she finally got her chance when the research vessel Nautilus VII departed from Port Esperanza with a crew of twelve scientists and eight engineers. The mission had three objectives. First, to collect water samples from below 8,000 meters to search for extremophile bacteria that could survive in total darkness and crushing pressure. Second, to map the geological formations of the trench floor using the ship's advanced sonar array, codenamed "Echo." Third, to deploy three autonomous underwater vehicles, or AUVs, named Triton, Calypso, and Nereid, which would spend six months gathering data on deep-sea currents. The descent began on March 22nd. Dr. Kenji Nakamura, the expedition's marine biologist, was the first to notice something unusual on the sonar display at 6,500 meters: a massive structure that appeared to be organic, roughly 400 meters long and 90 meters wide. It was not moving, but it was emitting a faint bioluminescent glow detected by the ship's spectral sensors. "That's not a geological formation," Dr. Nakamura said quietly. "It has a cellular structure." Chief Engineer Rosa Delgado maneuvered the Triton AUV closer. The high-definition cameras revealed an organism unlike anything in the biological record: a colonial organism resembling a vast, translucent web, anchored to the trench wall by thousands of filament-like roots. Dr. Nakamura named it Abyssal Veil, or in scientific terms, Velum abyssalis. Analysis of the water samples near the Abyssal Veil revealed extraordinary chemistry. The organism was performing a form of chemosynthesis using hydrogen sulfide from nearby hydrothermal vents, but it was also absorbing trace metals including manganese and cobalt from the surrounding seawater. Dr. Liang

or in scientific terms, Velum abyssalis. Analysis of the water samples near the Abyssal Veil revealed extraordinary chemistry. The organism was performing a form of chemosynthesis using hydrogen sulfide from nearby hydrothermal vents, but it was also absorbing trace metals including manganese and cobalt from the surrounding seawater. Dr. Liang Wei, the expedition's biochemist, estimated that the organism was at least 12,000 years old based on isotope analysis. Captain Solano made the decision to limit direct contact with the organism to protect it. They deployed Calypso at a safe distance of 200 meters to monitor the Abyssal Veil over the following months. The Nereid AUV continued its original mission of mapping the trench floor. The expedition returned to Port Esperanza on June 3rd, 2024, carrying 847 water samples, 12 terabytes of sonar data, and the discovery that would rewrite marine biology textbooks. Dr. Nakamura's paper on Velum abyssalis was published in the journal Nature Oceanic Science six months later and has been cited over 3,000 times. Captain Solano remarked in her expedition log: "We went to the bottom of the ocean expecting to find rocks and darkness. Instead, we found something alive, ancient, and beautiful. The deep sea still has secrets we cannot imagine."
